description:
Problem: the verdict job grants id-token: write job-wide (.github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml:69-73), so ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN and _URL are in the environment of every run step, including the attempt loop that starts the reviewer. Yama ptrace_scope 1 blocks /proc/<pid>/mem but not /proc/<pid>/environ, which needs only READ mode for a same-user process (security/yama/yama_lsm.c checks PTRACE_MODE_ATTACH only; fs/proc/base.c environ_open uses PTRACE_MODE_READ). actions/runner sets the request token to the same value as ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN (ScriptHandler.cs:318, NodeScriptActionHandler.cs:57,69), so a leak grants Actions service access for the job's lifetime. Redaction matches only literal or control-split values, so any encoding defeats it. The 2026-10-25 single-job decision record accepted this risk because the value is redacted; that premise is false.

Outcome (owner D2): the tailscale/github-action step authenticates with oauth-client-id and oauth-secret from the oracle environment secrets TS_OAUTH_CI_CLIENT_ID and TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET (tags tag:oracle-ci); the job drops id-token: write; the OAuth secret appears only in that step; both disk scans and redact-check include TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET; the isolation step fails closed if ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN is present in its environment; the decision record is corrected (redaction is accident hygiene, not a control; the request token is the runtime token; the OIDC acceptance is withdrawn).

Decision gates:
1. Before editing, confirm with gh secret list --env oracle (names only) that TS_OAUTH_CI_CLIENT_ID and TS_OAUTH_CI_SECRET exist. If not, set this item blocked with the owner setup steps and continue other items.
2. Confirm the pinned tailscale action supports oauth-secret with tags; if an upgrade is needed, pin the new version by full SHA and record why.
3. Read the action source at the pinned SHA and confirm it leaves no runner-user-readable copy of the secret or derived auth key; if it does, add that path to both disk scans before merging.

Item guardrails: no change to tag:oracle-ci ACLs, the gateway or other secrets; never echo a secret; keep the job's other permissions exactly; the owner deletes TS_AUDIENCE and the old TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID only after the live run, on request.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. Never use git stash (refs/stash is shared across worktrees). Commit as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, staging explicit paths only; no git add -A, no --no-verify, no SKIP, no agent trailers. Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, code) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Before publishing run make docs-reference-inventory-check, make doc-contracts-guard and make pr-preflight, and self-review with the code review action, fixing every Critical and Required finding. Publish only with make pr-open: never gh pr create, a raw push-and-open, or a PR-body override line; if make pr-open refuses, stop and report the exact refusal instead of routing around it. Until oracle-omp-pin-single-source-20261026 merges, make pr-open may run only with PATH prefixed by the darwin-arm64 omp 18.12.1 build whose SHA-256 that item records, verified with shasum immediately before use; never any other side-loaded omp. Close out only with oracle SHIP on the exact head, every oracle thread answered (reply naming the fixing SHA, then resolve) and make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge, a stand-in, an adjudication, or a ruleset or settings change. Never print tokens, keys, or the gateway URL or hostname; never spend model quota outside the review harness. Owner decisions are recorded in context and in the decisions file; a step that would contradict one stops and asks the owner.
